value.lineage: MINPACK (1980, Argonne National Laboratory): Levenberg-Marquardt least squares (LMDER/LMDIF/LMSTR) and Powell hybrid dogleg for nonlinear equations (HYBRD/HYBRJ), with CHKDER Jacobian checking; ancestor of scipy.optimize.leastsq/fsolve

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: curve fitting and root finding for nonlinear models, robustly, in 1980 Fortran

value.built_to: find x minimising sum of squares of m nonlinear functions, or solving n nonlinear equations, from a user function with or without an analytic Jacobian
value.pressure: ill-conditioned Jacobians, expensive function evaluations, users who cannot write a correct derivative (hence CHKDER)
value.success_means: convergence to a solution within the user's tolerances with a bounded number of function evaluations; the ANL-80-74 test set

ANCESTRY.value: MINPACK (1980, Argonne National Laboratory): Levenberg-Marquardt least squares (LMDER/LMDIF/LMSTR) and Powell hybrid dogleg for nonlinear equations (HYBRD/HYBRJ), with CHKDER Jacobian checking; ancestor of scipy.optimize.leastsq/fsolve

cut.note: two trust-region methods over a shared QR: least squares (LM: the step solves a damped system whose damping is chosen so the scaled step has length ~delta) and nonlinear equations (Powell hybrid: a dogleg between the Gauss-Newton and steepest-descent steps, with the Jacobian updated by Broyden rank-one and re-evaluated only when progress stalls); both accept a step by the ratio of actual to predicted reduction and move delta by fixed factors; the ancestor of scipy's leastsq and fsolve

organs.human_name: lmpar (1-264): parl / paru from the Gauss-Newton step and the gradient; the qrsolv iteration; 'abs(dxnorm-delta) .le. 0.1*delta' or 10 iterations
organs.mechanism: first solve the undamped (par = 0) least-squares step from the QR; if its scaled norm is within delta (10 percent slack) accept par = 0; else bracket par: a lower bound from the derivative of the step norm (parl, zero if the Jacobian is rank deficient) and an upper bound from the gradient norm over delta (paru); iterate at most 10 times: solve the damped system by qrsolv (a sequence of Givens rotations on R with sqrt(par) D appended), evaluate fp = ||D x|| - delta, stop if |fp| <= 0.1 delta, else take a Newton correction on 1/||D x||, update the bracket by the sign of fp, and set par = max(parl, par + parc)
organs.input: R, the permutation, Q'b, the scaling D, delta, the previous par
organs.output: par, x(par), and the Cholesky factor S
organs.state: none across calls except par as a warm start
assumptions: ||D x(par)|| is decreasing and convex in par (Hebden / More: so the Newton iteration on its reciprocal converges monotonically); 10 iterations and a 10 percent tolerance suffice because the outer loop tolerates an inexact radius
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: the trust-region subproblem for least squares solved to 10 percent in a handful of cheap rotations rather than by an eigen-decomposition
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: rank-deficient Jacobians set parl = 0 and the exceptional-case exit accepts a step inside the region; the 10-iteration cap returns 'the best value obtained so far'
organs.human_prior: Hebden 1973; More 1978 'The Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm: implementation and theory' (the paper this code implements)

organs.human_name: lmder (330-440): actred, prered, dirder, ratio; 'if (ratio .gt. p25) go to 240'; temp = p5*dirder/(dirder + p5*actred); delta = pnorm/p5 on ratio >= 0.75; the info 1-8 tests
organs.mechanism: after a step p of scaled length pnorm: actual reduction = 1 - (fnorm1/fnorm)^2 (or -1 if the residual grew tenfold); predicted reduction from the linear model = ||J p||^2/fnorm^2 + 2 par pnorm^2/fnorm^2, directional derivative likewise; ratio = actual/predicted; if ratio <= 0.25 shrink delta to temp * min(delta, 10 pnorm) with temp from a quadratic interpolation of the residual along p (clamped to [0.1, 0.5]) and divide par by temp; if ratio >= 0.75 (or par = 0) set delta = 2 pnorm and halve par; accept the step only if ratio >= 1e-4; convergence tests on |actred| and prered (ftol), delta vs xtol ||D x||, and the scaled gradient (gtol); the first iteration caps delta at pnorm
organs.input: the step, the residual norms, par
assumptions: the quadratic model predicts the reduction well within delta; the actual/predicted ratio is a reliable measure of model quality (the trust-region premise)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: global convergence without a line search; the radius adapts to the model's local accuracy
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: constants (0.25, 0.75, 1e-4, factor 100 for the initial delta) are the paper's; a bad scaling D (mode 1 uses the Jacobian column norms) changes the geometry of delta
organs.human_prior: More 1978 section 4; the same acceptance rule is in every later trust-region code
organs.source_boundary: the inner loop of lmder (shared verbatim by lmdif and lmstr)

organs.human_name: dogleg (60-175): the Gauss-Newton solve from R packed by rows with a diagonal repair; qnorm <= delta -> return; sgnorm (the Cauchy step length); alpha from the boundary quadratic
organs.mechanism: solve R x = Q'b for the Gauss-Newton step (a zero diagonal entry is replaced by eps times the largest entry in its row: a cheap rank repair); if its scaled norm is within delta take it; else compute the scaled gradient and the Cauchy (steepest-descent minimiser) step length sgnorm; if sgnorm >= delta take the gradient step scaled to delta; else take the point on the segment from the Cauchy point to the Gauss-Newton point that lies on the boundary (alpha from a closed-form quadratic)
assumptions: the piecewise-linear dogleg path approximates the true trust-region minimiser well enough for the ratio test to accept most steps
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: one triangular solve and a few norms per step; no damping parameter search
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the diagonal repair silently changes a singular system; the path is not the exact subproblem minimiser (Powell 1970 argued it need not be)
organs.human_prior: Powell 1970 'A hybrid method for nonlinear equations'

organs.human_name: hybrd (208-440): jeval, ncsuc / ncfail, nslow1 / nslow2, 'if (ncfail .eq. 2) go to 290', r1updt / r1mpyq; delta halved on ratio < 0.1, raised to 2 pnorm on ratio >= 0.5 or two successes
organs.mechanism: the Jacobian is formed by forward differences (fdjac1, banded if ml/mu say so) and QR-factored once per outer iteration; inside, each accepted step updates the factored Jacobian by the Broyden secant correction (a rank-one update of R carried through Q by Givens rotations, r1updt/r1mpyq) rather than re-evaluating; the outer loop re-evaluates only when two consecutive steps failed (ncfail = 2); progress monitors count iterations with actual reduction below 0.001 (nslow1, ten -> info 5) and Jacobian evaluations with reduction below 0.1 (nslow2, five -> info 4); delta is halved on ratio < 0.1 and raised on ratio >= 0.5 or after two successes
assumptions: secant information from accepted steps is good enough to avoid n function evaluations per iteration; failure to reduce the residual twice means the secant Jacobian has drifted
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: n-fold fewer function evaluations per iteration than a finite-difference Newton
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the monitors terminate with 'not making good progress' rather than diverging; the secant update can make R singular (r1updt reports sing; the dogleg's diagonal repair copes)
organs.source_boundary: hybrd's outer/inner loops (hybrj is the analytic-Jacobian twin)

rejected_cuts.candidate: qrfac (Householder QR with column pivoting), qrsolv, r1updt, r1mpyq, qform, enorm (the overflow-safe norm), dpmpar (machine constants)
rejected_cuts.evidence: NOT READ; the linear-algebra substrate; enorm's three-accumulator scaling is a small mechanism of its own, unread

rejected_cuts.candidate: lmdif (finite-difference LM), lmstr (row-wise storage), the *1 driver wrappers, chkder (Jacobian check), fdjac1/fdjac2, the ex/ drivers and file01-23 outputs
rejected_cuts.note: ex/ holds the test problems and reference outputs: an oracle for a Stage C run

rejected_cuts.evidence: the damping search (lmpar) and the acceptance/radius logic (lmder) are separable; the latter is shared with the hybrid method

pressures.condition: an organism minimises ||F(x)|| (or solves F(x) = 0) where each F is expensive; the linear model is good only locally; the start may be far from the solution; the score is evaluations to a tolerance and robustness to bad starts
pressures.resource_or_constraint: function evaluations; a fixed QR per Jacobian
pressures.failure_condition: divergence from a poor start (pure Gauss-Newton), or evaluations wasted on a Jacobian that has not changed
pressures.world_punishes: full steps regardless of model quality; re-evaluating the Jacobian every iteration
pressures.world_rewards: a trust radius adapted by actual/predicted reduction; secant updates with a failure-triggered refresh
pressures.observable_consequence: function evaluations and success rate over the More-Garbow-Hillstrom problem set (the ex/ drivers) for LM vs Gauss-Newton, and hybrid vs finite-difference Newton, from the standard and 10x starts
pressures.trivial_shortcuts: a start within the Newton basin
pressures.cheat_control: an organism given the exact Hessian must reach the tolerance in the fewest iterations; Gauss-Newton without a region must diverge on some 10x starts; the hybrid with re-evaluation every step must use ~n times more evaluations at the same success: the world must show all three
pressures.purpose_separated_from_pressure: PURPOSE: nonlinear least squares and equations (More, Garbow, Hillstrom 1980)

ancestry_edges.to: More 1978 (LM implementation); Hebden 1973 (the par iteration); Powell 1970 (hybrid dogleg); Broyden 1965
ancestry_edges.note: from the source comments and the record

unexplained: nothing ran; ex/ is the oracle
residue.note: the four mechanisms that make the two methods robust are located and separated from the linear algebra
